html:
A caravan town in southeastern Mauritania which, after the decline of Koumbi Saleh in the 13th century, became the main southern end of the desert routes to the Mali Empire.

Ibn Battuta stayed there in 1352 on his way to Mali and wrote with surprise about the freedom of its women. Its scholars kept libraries of manuscripts, and its houses are known for the red and white designs painted by women on their walls. Its trade later moved to Timbuktu. It is one of the four old towns of Mauritania listed by UNESCO in 1996, with Chinguetti.
sum: A caravan town in southeastern Mauritania which, after the decline of Koumbi Saleh in the 13th century, became the main southern end of the desert routes to the Mali Empire.
